metaTitle: Electrician RPL: Fast Track Cert III (UEE30820)
metaDescription: Experienced electrician? Fast track your UEE30820 Cert III in Electrotechnology through RPL, the qualification behind an electrical licence. Free check.
heroIntro: The UEE30820 Certificate III in Electrotechnology Electrician is the qualification behind an Australian electrical licence. If you have solid electrical work experience, in Australia or overseas, RPL recognises it so you only train and get assessed where you have gaps, then sit the final practical (Capstone) assessment.
whoIsItFor:
This pathway is for people who already do electrical work but don't hold the Australian trade qualification:

  • Overseas-qualified electricians working in Australia
  • Electrical trade assistants with long, broad experience under a licensed electrician
  • Apprentices who didn't complete and kept working in the industry
  • Electrical workers holding a restricted licence who want the full trade

It replaces the older UEE30811. You need substantial, recent and varied electrical experience: wiring and installing circuits, fault finding, testing, switchboards, and working to AS/NZS 3000 (the Wiring Rules). Electrical work is high-risk, so RPL here is strict and evidence-heavy.
evidenceExamples:
Assessors need detailed, verifiable evidence of the electrical work you've done. Typical evidence:

  • A detailed statement of service or reference from a licensed electrician or electrical contractor
  • Photos and videos of installations: rough-in, fit-off, switchboards, three-phase work, fault finding
  • Test results and records you've completed (insulation resistance, earth continuity, polarity)
  • Overseas trade qualifications and licences, with certified translations
  • Payslips, employment contracts or tax records showing time in electrical roles
  • Any Australian tickets: White Card, CPR/LVR, working at heights

Expect a detailed competency conversation and practical assessments, then the Capstone assessment, which is done in person.
licensingInfo:
Electrical licences are issued by state and territory regulators, never by training organisations. In every state, the UEE30820 qualification including the Capstone (final practical) assessment is the core requirement for an unrestricted electrician's licence. Some regulators also require a period of supervised work. Regulators include:

  • New South Wales: NSW Fair Trading
  • Victoria: Energy Safe Victoria
  • Queensland: the Electrical Safety Office
  • Western Australia: Building and Energy
  • South Australia: Consumer and Business Services
  • Tasmania, ACT and NT: CBOS, Access Canberra and the NT licensing board

There is no shortcut around the Capstone. RPL can cover the units you're already competent in, but the Capstone must be passed in person. If you trained overseas, other skills-recognition pathways may also apply. Talk to us about your situation before you start.
description:
The UEE30820 Certificate III in Electrotechnology Electrician is the national trade qualification for electricians. It covers selecting, installing, setting up, testing, fault finding, repairing and maintaining electrical systems and equipment in buildings and premises, to the Australian Standards and the Wiring Rules.

It is a large qualification built on weighting points, with a substantial core and general electives, and it includes the Capstone assessment that licensing regulators rely on. It replaces UEE30811.
jobOpportunity: Solar and battery installer (with the relevant accreditation)
Electrical inspector or estimator, with experience
deliveryMode: Online evidence + in-person practical and Capstone
imageAlt: Electrician testing a switchboard with a multimeter

faqs.q: Can I get an electrician qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have substantial electrical work experience. RPL covers the units you can prove you're competent in, with gap training for the rest. You must still pass the Capstone practical assessment in person before you can apply for a licence.

faqs.q: Does UEE30820 RPL get me an electrical licence?
faqs.a: The qualification, including the Capstone, is the main requirement for an electrician's licence in every state. The licence itself is issued by your state regulator, which may also require supervised work experience. We'll explain your state's steps when you apply.

faqs.q: How long does electrician RPL take?
faqs.a: It usually takes 3 to 6 months, because the qualification is large and includes practical and Capstone assessments. Your evidence and any gap training affect the timeline.

faqs.q: I'm an electrician from overseas. Can I use RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, overseas experience can be assessed. You'll need strong evidence of the work you've done and how it compares with Australian standards. Depending on your situation, an offshore skills pathway may also be an option, so ask us before you begin.
The evidence portfolio and interview are online. Practical assessments and the Capstone are done in person at an approved assessment venue.

The cost depends on how many units your evidence covers, the gap training you need and the Capstone. It's usually far cheaper than a four-year apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check for a clear quote.

faqs.q: I studied UEE30811. Do I need UEE30820?
faqs.a: UEE30811 was replaced by UEE30820. If you completed UEE30811 it remains valid. If you didn't finish it, any new enrolment or RPL is in UEE30820, and completed units may be credited.

metaTitle: Air Conditioning & Refrigeration RPL Fast Track (UEE32225)
metaDescription: HVAC tech without the paperwork? Get your UEE32225 Cert III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration through RPL, the ARC licence pathway. Free check.
heroIntro: The UEE32225 Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration is the trade qualification for HVAC and refrigeration technicians, and the main pathway to a full ARC refrigerant handling licence. It replaces UEE32220. If you already install and service air conditioning or refrigeration systems, RPL can recognise that experience.
whoIsItFor:
• Air conditioning installers and service technicians
  • Refrigeration mechanics working on commercial or industrial systems
  • HVAC workers holding a restricted or split-system licence who want the full trade
  • Overseas-trained refrigeration and air conditioning mechanics

Candidates usually have several years of hands-on HVAC/R work: installing, commissioning, servicing and fault finding on split systems, ducted systems, coolrooms and commercial refrigeration, including refrigerant handling and the electrical side of the equipment.
evidenceExamples:
• A detailed reference or statement of service from a licensed refrigeration or air conditioning contractor
  • Photos and videos of installations, brazing, pressure testing, evacuation and commissioning
  • Service and commissioning records, logbooks and fault reports you've completed
  • Any ARC licence or restricted electrical licence you hold
  • Overseas qualifications, with certified translations
  • Payslips or tax records showing time in the trade

Practical assessments are usually needed for the hands-on refrigeration and electrical units.
licensingInfo:
Two kinds of licence matter for HVAC/R work:

  • Refrigerant handling: handling fluorocarbon refrigerants needs a licence from the Australian Refrigeration Council (ARC). This qualification is the pathway to the full refrigeration and air conditioning licence.
  • Electrical work: disconnecting and reconnecting equipment is electrical work, regulated by your state's electrical regulator. Some states issue a restricted electrical licence for this, with their own requirements.

Tell us which ARC licence and state electrical licence you're aiming for, and we'll check what the qualification and electives cover.
description:
The UEE32225 Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration covers installing, commissioning, servicing, fault finding and repairing refrigeration and air conditioning systems, from domestic split systems to commercial and industrial plant, including safe refrigerant handling and the electrical work involved.

It is the current version of the qualification, replacing UEE32220, and is built on core and elective weighting points.
imageAlt: HVAC technician servicing an outdoor air conditioning unit

faqs.q: Can I get the UEE32225 Air Conditioning and Refrigeration qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have substantial hands-on HVAC/R experience. RPL covers what you can prove, with gap training and practical assessments for the rest.
UEE32220 was superseded by UEE32225 Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration. If you already hold UEE32220 it remains valid. New enrolments and RPL are in UEE32225.

faqs.q: Will I get an ARC licence?
faqs.a: This qualification is the pathway to the full ARC refrigeration and air conditioning licence. You apply to the ARC once you're qualified.
Usually 3 to 6 months, depending on your evidence, any gap training and practical assessment bookings.
Your evidence and interview are online. The practical refrigeration and electrical assessments are done in person.
It depends on how many units your evidence covers and what gap training you need. RPL is usually much cheaper than a full apprenticeship. Ask for a free eligibility check.
